question: does removing the measured 45 mm take-waypoint command error improve the score the demo video is held on?
answer: NO. No arm beats shipped. Neither knob is adopted; both stay at the shipped default and both are proven inert there.
not_claimed: harm. 15-18/50 sits inside the scatter the CUTLERY_SQUEEZE sweep already recorded for this quantity at n=10 ('fork_placed is 1-3 of 10 across the entire sweep, which at n=10 is noise'). The verdict is NO MEASURED IMPROVEMENT, not 'worse'.

knobs_inert_at_default.basis: evidence/taker_servo.json, run at both defaults AFTER the two structural edits to _handoff: reproduces_published PASS, abs_delta_mm 0.0 on all ten seeds against the pinned shipped column [158.9,149.4,14.0,54.6,70.2,83.0,159.8,35.9,143.6,20.3]
knobs_inert_at_default.why_it_matters: an edit that changes the shipped robot cannot be called off-by-default

knobs_are_live_when_on.basis: evidence/taker_servo_planatopen.json: plan_err_mm 43.9-46.5 -> 3.0-9.5 on all ten seeds, and reproduces_published FAILS in that arm -- which is the CORRECT outcome, because the arm changed the robot
knobs_are_live_when_on.why_it_matters: a knob whose ON arm still reproduces the shipped column is not connected to anything

arms_differ.why_it_matters: arms that produce an identical per-seed column are the same experiment run four times
